describes: The spellings the workflow's prompts and tools must agree on: the tracker label that marks a product change's epic and every one of its tasks (`specChangeLabel`), the prefix of each capability's scenario and NFR IDs (`specIdPrefixes`), the three label vocabularies a run leaves in the tracker so that `bd count` can show what recurs across runs (`assetLabels`, `foundAtLabels`, `rerouteLabels`), the instant from which a found issue must carry a found-at label (`foundAtLabelsSince`) and the command that files a found issue with them (`foundIssueCommand`), the prefix of the label that counts how many runs have found an issue (`seenLabelPrefix`), the type and priority every issue is filed with (`issueTypes`, `issuePriorities`), the length of the hash a test's metadata carries for each artifact it was written against and the layers a test may declare (`testTraceHashLength`, `testTraceLayers`; the header of `scripts/test-trace.mjs`), the layers whose tests count toward a scenario's happy-path and negative obligation (`traceObligationLayers`; the header of `tools/trace/trace.ts`), and the key of the git trailer that records an architect's decision to remove, skip or weaken a test (`testInventoryTrailer`; the header of `scripts/check-test-inventory.mjs`).
whyThisFileExists: A spelling written in a register entry, six skills and an agent is eight copies, and the stale one is the one a reader finds. Each value here is read by more than one prompt or tool, or is written by people and agents into the tracker, a test or a commit, so it has one home, which each of them cites by key (`CLAUDE.md` § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth). `docs/decisions.md` § D-03 made the first of them a key of the policy; § D-27 split the policy by who reads each key and who may change it, and these are the keys every stage of the workflow reads.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run openspec:check holds `specChangeLabel`: every skill and agent that spells the label cites the key, and every one that cites the key spells its current value. It also holds `specIdPrefixes`: it refuses the key missing, with no `Means` sibling, a capability with no prefix, and a prefix that is not a string of capital letters and digits, is `NFR`, or is another capability's, and reads the prefixes to refuse a scenario or NFR requirement header without its capability's ID, one ID on two headers, and an ID an archived delta gave another title; mise run openspec:selftest runs each refusal on a fixture, asserting the reason it reports. mise run calculator:test holds `testTraceHashLength` and `testTraceLayers`, with `prReviewIssuePattern` of `tools/policy/pr-review.json` as the shape of a task's ID in a test's name: it reads every test file through scripts/test-trace.mjs, which reads the three from the policy and refuses a hash of another length, a layer the key does not list, a level above its layer's default with no reason, and a policy without them; mise run tests:selftest runs its refusals on fixture trees carrying a copy of the policy, and mise run tests:trace:selftest refuses a policy with no hash length and holds that the live one reads. mise run trace:check holds that each hash a test carries is current and that each scenario and NFR ID it names resolves, reading the reader's three keys through scripts/test-trace.mjs and `prReviewIssuePattern` also as the shape of the task IDs a commit's subject names; it holds `traceObligationLayers`: it counts only a test at one of those layers toward a scenario's happy-path and negative obligation, and refuses a layer the key names that `testTraceLayers` does not list; mise run trace:selftest runs each refusal on a fixture tree carrying a copy of the policy, one with that key doctored. mise run tests:inventory:check holds `testInventoryTrailer`: it reads the key from the policy at HEAD, refuses its run when the key is missing or is not a word git reads as a trailer's key, and clears a removed, skipped or weakened test only with a trailer whose key is exactly that value, case included; mise run tests:inventory:selftest refuses a policy at HEAD without it and holds that the live one spells one. No gate holds that a capability that is removed keeps its key here, so that no later capability takes its prefix (the header of scripts/check-openspec.mjs). mise run beads:check holds `assetLabels`: it refuses an open issue filed `discovered-from` that carries no label this key lists, reading the list from the policy and spelling none of its values, and mise run beads:selftest runs that refusal over a fixture export and a copy of the policy, including one with the key removed and one with a label renamed; mise run workflows:selftest refuses a kind of `tools/policy/agent-workflows.json` that is not an `assetLabels` key. mise run beads:check also holds `issueTypes`: it refuses an issue that is not closed whose type no row names, reading the types from the policy and spelling none, and refuses a policy without the key or with a row that names no type; mise run beads:selftest runs each refusal, including one with a type renamed here. No gate holds `issuePriorities`: no check can tell which row an issue fits, and `bd` itself refuses a priority outside 0 to 4 (`bd create -p 5 --dry-run` exits 1 with an invalid-priority error). mise run beads:check also holds `foundAtLabels` and `foundAtLabelsSince`: it refuses an open issue filed `discovered-from` whose `created_at` is not before that instant and that carries no label `foundAtLabels` lists, reading both from the policy and spelling neither, and refuses a policy without either key, with an empty list, or with a cut-off that is not an instant in UTC ending in `Z`; mise run beads:selftest runs each refusal, including one with a found-at label renamed here and one with the cut-off moved back onto an issue it exempted. No gate holds `rerouteLabels`: the prompts cite the key and spell none of its values, and a reroute label records that a change went back, so its absence is the normal case and no presence rule can hold it. No gate holds `foundIssueCommand`: `bead` and `change-build` cite it and spell no part of it, and nothing refuses a prompt that spells the command again. No gate holds `seenLabelPrefix`: nothing refuses an issue that carries two counts or one that skips a number, and `CLAUDE.md` cites the key and spells no part of it.
whatItDoesNOTDo: It does not hold a rule about how a run proceeds, which lives in CLAUDE.md or in the skill that runs it: when a label, a type or a priority is applied is CLAUDE.md § The task store and § Product work runs as OpenSpec-format changes, and who reads the counts is `.claude/skills/change-finalize/SKILL.md` § 9. Report. It computes nothing: `bd count` does the counting, and what it counts is defined once, in count-index.md § Rates and metrics. It holds no ID and no counter: the next free ID of a prefix is derived from the specs, as the header of `scripts/check-openspec.mjs` says, and never stored here, and how many runs have found an issue is a label on that issue, of which this record holds only the prefix. It holds no rule of the test-metadata convention and no hash: the grammar of a test's name and `// trace:` line, and what each hash is taken over, are the header of `scripts/test-trace.mjs`, and each hash is in the test that cites it. It holds no decision to remove, skip or weaken a test, which is a trailer on a commit of the branch, and not the grammar of that trailer, which is the header of `scripts/check-test-inventory.mjs`. It holds no tunable size or bound, which is `tools/policy/agent-workflows.json`'s, and nothing only a person may change, which is `tools/policy/pr-review.json`'s and `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`'s.
provenance: Split out of `tools/policy.json` on 2026-10-02 by D-27 (asdlc-openspec-umg3), each key with its value and its `Means` as that file held them at 962358c (`git show 962358c:tools/policy.json`). That file was written 2026-09-23 under D-03 (asdlc-openspec-4gp), which moved the label's spelling there out of D-02. `assetLabels`, `foundAtLabels` and `rerouteLabels` came with D-06. `specIdPrefixes` came with D-13 (asdlc-openspec-j09.3) on 2026-09-28, with the prefixes the maintainer chose. `testTraceHashLength` and `testTraceLayers` came with D-13 (asdlc-openspec-j09.5) on 2026-09-28, each with its reason in its `Means`, and `traceObligationLayers` with D-13 (asdlc-openspec-j09.7) the same day, from the strategy's text. `testInventoryTrailer` came with D-13 (asdlc-openspec-j09.9) on 2026-09-28, with its reason in its `Means`. `issueTypes` and `issuePriorities` came with D-29 (asdlc-openspec-6g6w) on 2026-10-03, with the types, the scale and the gate the maintainer chose, and `foundIssueCommand` gained its `-t` and `-p` the same day. `foundAtLabelsSince` came with D-41 (asdlc-openspec-sbp) on 2026-10-04, at the cut-off the maintainer chose. `seenLabelPrefix` came with D-43 (asdlc-openspec-4myz) on 2026-10-05, the label the maintainer chose. Each key carries its date and its evidence in its `Means`.
specChangeLabelMeans: The tracker label on a product change's epic and on every one of its tasks (docs/decisions.md § D-02, item 3). change-propose puts it on the epic and the children inherit it; the general sweeps of the queue exclude it (`bd ready --exclude-label` in the bead skill and the fan-out-work agent), and change-plan, change-build, change-verify and change-finalize find the epic by it. Changing it here strands every open change: relabel their epics and tasks in the same change, and respell the label in every skill and agent that cites this key, which `mise run openspec:check` names. Decided 2026-09-23 with D-02; moved here 2026-09-23 by D-03.
specIdPrefixesMeans: The prefix every scenario and NFR ID of a capability carries: each key a capability (a directory under openspec/specs/, or under a change's specs/), each value its prefix. The ID rules, what `mise run openspec:check` refuses and where the next free ID comes from are the header of scripts/check-openspec.mjs, their one home under docs/decisions.md § D-13. A change that adds a capability adds its key here in the same change; renaming a prefix re-keys every header and every test that names it. Where it loses: a reader who meets `[CLS-014]` in a test name looks the prefix up here to learn its capability, where the full capability name would have said so. Decided 2026-09-28 with D-13, the prefixes chosen by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.3).
testTraceHashLengthMeans: How many characters of an artifact's lowercase hex sha256 a test's `// trace:` line carries as the version of that artifact it was written against: a scenario's block with its requirement's statement, an NFR requirement's block, a Binding Surface or a contract file (the header of scripts/test-trace.mjs, the convention's one home under docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 17). A hash is compared only with the current hash of the same block, so it is a version stamp and not an identity: 12 characters leave one edit in 2^48 unnoticed, where all 64 would make a trace line 52 characters longer for each artifact it cites. Changing it makes every hash in every test the wrong length, which `mise run calculator:test` then refuses: rewrite them from `node scripts/test-trace.mjs cite` in the same change. Where it loses: an edit whose block hashes to the same 12 characters leaves its tests current, where the full 64 would not. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.5).
testTraceLayersMeans: The layers a test may declare in its `// trace:` metadata, each key a layer and each value its default orchestration level, as docs/test-strategy.md § Environment orchestration rules gives them; `null` where the level is declared per test, as it is for a fitness function. A test at a level above its layer's default records why, and a test at or below it records no reason; scripts/test-trace.mjs, whose header is the convention's one home, refuses either slip and a layer this key does not list. Mutation is not a layer: a mutation run references the suite it targets (docs/test-strategy.md § Traceability, rule 7). Levels 2 and 3 are not adopted until a product needs them (docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 17), so an integration test here runs at level 1, below its default, and records nothing. The layer of each of the calculator's test files was the maintainer's choice (asdlc-openspec-j09.5's notes). Adding a layer here lets a test declare it; removing one strands every test that declares it, which `mise run calculator:test` then refuses. Where it loses: a default changed here moves the level of every test that states none, without a line of any test changing. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.5).
testInventoryTrailerMeans: The key of the git trailer that records an architect's decision to remove, skip or weaken a test on a branch (docs/test-strategy.md § Test ownership). `mise run tests:inventory:check` (scripts/check-test-inventory.mjs, whose header is the rule's one home under docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 17) compares a branch's tests with its merge base with `origin/main`, and refuses each test removed, given a skip, todo or only, or left with fewer assertions, unless a commit on the branch carries `<this key>: <remove|skip|weaken> <file> "<test name>" <reason>` in the last paragraph of its message, where git reads trailers, with this key spelled exactly, case included; that header holds the grammar. The key names the role the strategy gives the decision, the architect, who is the build workflow's triage together with the session running change-build (D-13, item 16). Changing it leaves every trailer written under the old spelling on an open branch unread, so the gate refuses what it cleared; a trailer already on the trunk is never read again, since the gate reads only a branch's own commits. Where it loses: any commit's author can write the trailer, so it records that a decision was made and why, not who made it; the pull-request reviewer and the person merging read it. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.9).
traceObligationLayersMeans: The layers whose tests count toward a scenario's obligation of at least one happy-path test and one negative test: docs/test-strategy.md § Scenario coverage counts functional, integration, contract and E2E tests, and not unit tests. Each is a key of `testTraceLayers`. `mise run trace:check` refuses a scenario with no happy-path or no negative test at one of these layers, unless the ratchet baseline lists that obligation or the scenario's happy-path test declares its negative not applicable, and refuses a layer here that `testTraceLayers` does not list (the header of tools/trace/trace.ts). Fitness is not here: a fitness function proves an NFR, whose scenarios owe neither test (docs/decisions.md § D-13, item 14). Where it loses: a scenario proved only by a thorough unit test counts as unproved until a functional test repeats it. Adding `unit` lets a unit test meet the obligation, which the strategy refuses. Taken from the strategy's text, which D-13 adopted, on 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-j09.7).

assetLabels.asset:docs: a document that is neither the register nor the living spec: a README, a page under docs/, count-index.md
assetLabels.asset:environment: what a session runs on: the worktree script and its briefing template, the toolchain's versions, the harness's settings, the dev container
assetLabels.asset:gate: a gate, a hook, a test runner, or a job that runs one (git-hooks.yml, .github/workflows/verify.yml)
assetLabels.asset:product: the product's code and its tests, under apps/
assetLabels.asset:prompt: CLAUDE.md, a skill, an agent, or a workflow script a skill runs
assetLabels.asset:register: the register: docs/decisions.md, frozen at D-59, and the records under docs/decisions/
assetLabels.asset:spec: the living spec under openspec/specs/, or a change's proposal and delta specs
assetLabels.asset:tool: an emitter or a helper under tools/ or scripts/ that is not a gate

assetLabelsMeans: What an issue a run files `discovered-from` would fix: one label for each kind of file it would change, each key the label and each value what it covers (CLAUDE.md § The task store says when). Paired with its `foundAtLabels` label it is the recurrence signal the retired learning loop was to derive (docs/decisions.md § D-06): `bd count -l <a found-at label> --by-label` counts the pairs. An issue that fits none of these gets the label it needs added here first, with its date, in the change that files it. Renaming a label strands every issue that carries it: relabel them in the same change. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn); the eight values were fitted to the issues discovered from asdlc-openspec-zgh.

foundAtLabels.found:bead: while an issue was worked through the bead skill, or a lane of the fan-out-work agent
foundAtLabels.found:review: by looking back at a run after it ended: a prompt review, or a person or session reviewing a finished change

foundAtLabelsMeans: Where an issue a run files `discovered-from` was found: exactly one label, the stage that was running, each key the label and each value when it applies (CLAUDE.md § The task store says when). `found:review` is the count of what got through every stage and was caught only looking back. An issue filed before D-06 carries one only where its own text says which stage found it. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn), after a second opinion on the retirement pointed out that the loop's recurrence signal is the pair of where a correction was found and what it would fix.
foundAtLabelsSinceMeans: The instant from which an issue a run files `discovered-from` must carry a `foundAtLabels` label: `mise run beads:check` refuses an open issue filed `discovered-from` whose `created_at` is at or after it and that carries none, and exempts one created before it, which `foundAtLabelsMeans` says carries one only where its own text says which stage found it. It is an ISO 8601 instant in UTC ending in `Z`, the form `bd export` writes `created_at` in; the gate refuses one without the `Z`, which it would read in the local time of whoever runs it. The value is the `created_at` of asdlc-openspec-6dn, the issue that carries D-06 (`bd show asdlc-openspec-6dn --json`), the first instant the tracker records D-06 at. Moving it earlier refuses each open issue it exempted until that issue carries a label; moving it later exempts an issue filed after D-06. Where it loses: an issue filed before it stays exempt for as long as it is open, so on 2026-10-04 asdlc-openspec-0db, open, filed `discovered-from` at 2026-09-24T22:53:47Z and carrying no found-at label, is counted by kind and never by stage while the gate passes, where a presence check with no cut-off would refuse it until someone guessed its stage. And an issue filed after it but before D-06 reached the trunk, with pull request #27 at 2026-09-25T12:21:51Z, is held to a rule its filer's checkout did not yet state, where that later instant would exempt it; on 2026-10-04 the tracker held one, asdlc-openspec-dzi, filed by the session writing D-06 and labelled. Derived 2026-10-04 from asdlc-openspec-6dn, and chosen by the maintainer the same day from three candidates (asdlc-openspec-sbp; docs/decisions.md § D-41).
foundIssueCommand: bd create "<title>" -t <its type> -p <its priority> -l <the repo: label>,<its found-at label>,<its asset: labels> --deps discovered-from:<the issue or epic the run worked> --body-file <file> --silent
foundIssueCommandMeans: The command that files an issue a run finds outside its work, each `<...>` filled in: its title; its type and priority, the first rows of `issueTypes` and `issuePriorities` that fit it, which puts a found issue at 3 unless a higher row fits; the labels `CLAUDE.md` § The task store names, which are the `repo:` label naming where the work lands, the stage's label from `foundAtLabels` and one label from `assetLabels` for each kind of file it would change; the issue or epic the run worked, which `discovered-from` ties it to so `bd count` reads the pair; and the body from a file, as `CLAUDE.md` § Bash command style asks. `--silent` prints only the new id. `.claude/skills/bead/SKILL.md` § 4 and `.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 5 cite this key and spell no part of it, so the command changes here and nowhere else. Decided 2026-10-01 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-f69), moving it out of the two skills that each spelled it. `-t` and `-p` added 2026-10-03 by D-29 (asdlc-openspec-6g6w): before them a found issue took `bd`'s defaults, a task at 2, whatever it was.

issueTypes.when: A product change, run through the `change-*` skills. Only `change-propose` sets this type, on the epic it opens or on the issue that seeds it (docs/decisions.md § D-02, item 3); nothing else files one.
A person chooses between options, and nothing changes until they do: a `should-i-adopt` brief, or a question that begins "Decide". The work each option needs is filed once one is chosen.

Something already in the repository gives a wrong result, and a command shows it: a gate passes what it should refuse or refuses what it should pass, a script fails or writes the wrong output, or a document states what the code does not do. `bd lint` asks its body for `## Steps to Reproduce` as well as `## Acceptance Criteria`.

An agent investigates a question, and what lands is a finding written down, in a note, a document or the issues it files, not a change to what anything does. A choice among the options it finds is a person's, filed as a decision.

Adds something a person or a session cannot do here today: a new skill, agent, gate, emitter, script or check. A change to what the product does is not one: it goes to `change-propose`, which makes it an epic.
Upkeep that changes no behaviour and no rule: rewording, renaming, regenerating, moving, or removing what nothing reads. A rewording that corrects a document the code contradicts is a bug.
Everything the rows above leave: improving or extending something that exists, writing a document, or a step a person performs outside the repository.

issueTypesMeans: The type every issue is filed with: each row a type `bd create -t` takes and when it applies, tried in order, the first row that fits winning, so an issue that would fit two takes the earlier (`CLAUDE.md` § The task store says when a type is set). The type decides what `bd lint --help` asks the body to carry, and what `bd count --by-type` and `bd list --type` separate. `mise run beads:check` refuses an issue that is not closed whose type no row names, reading the rows here and spelling none, so `story` and `milestone`, which `bd create --help` also lists, are refused; a closed issue keeps the type it closed with. Adding a row lets an issue take its type, and moving one changes which of two rows wins; removing or renaming one refuses every open issue that carries it, so retype them in the same change. Where it loses: the line between feature, chore and task stays a filer's judgement, and the order settles only an issue that fits two rows, not one that two filers read differently. Decided 2026-10-03 with D-29 (asdlc-openspec-6g6w), the seven types the maintainer chose from the ones the tracker held that day.

issuePriorities.when: Work cannot proceed: the trunk fails `verify`, no session can start, or something is destroying work, a worktree, the tracker or a branch.

A safeguard fails silently: a gate, a guard or the pull-request reviewer passes or skips what it should refuse, or a tool drops output a session relies on. Every run until it is fixed can land wrong work and say nothing.

Planned work: what a person asked for, an epic and its tasks, and a failure that stops a workflow loudly. It is `bd`'s default, which a change's tasks take, since `change-plan` files them with no priority.

Found on the way, and nothing breaks while it waits: friction, or a wrong result nothing relies on, such as a document that misstates what the code does. An issue filed `discovered-from` another takes it unless a row above fits.
Someday: speculative, exploratory or cosmetic, and nothing gets worse if it is never done.

issuePrioritiesMeans: The priority every issue is filed with: each row a value `bd create -p` takes, 0 the highest, and when it applies, tried from 0 down, so an issue takes the highest row that fits (`CLAUDE.md` § The task store says when a priority is set). Each row says what leaving the issue undone costs, because the priority decides what is worked first: `bd ready` sorts by it unless told otherwise (`bd ready --help`), and the `bead` skill, `change-build` and the `fan-out-work` agent take what it lists first. No gate holds it, because no check can tell which row an issue fits. A row reworded here changes what every later filing reads and moves no issue already filed. Where it loses: friction that recurs is ranked by its size each time it is paid, so a cost every session pays, such as a hook that asks each edit of a file to rewrite rows the edit did not touch (asdlc-openspec-23bi), stays at 3, below all planned work, however many sessions it slows. Decided 2026-10-03 with D-29 (asdlc-openspec-6g6w), the scale the maintainer chose, fitted to how the tracker used each level that day (docs/decisions.md § D-29).

rerouteLabels.reroute:build: change-verify or change-finalize sent work back to change-build: a gap in the code, a finding the user made a new task, or a test trace:check refused after the archive
rerouteLabels.reroute:design: a later stage revised the design
rerouteLabels.reroute:plan: a later stage added a task to the epic
rerouteLabels.reroute:propose: a later stage revised the proposal or a delta spec

rerouteLabelsMeans: Labels on a product change's epic, one for each earlier stage a later stage sent the change back to, each key the label and each value when it applies (CLAUDE.md § Product work runs as OpenSpec-format changes says when). A label is a set: it records that the change went back, not how often. `bd count -t epic -l <specChangeLabel> --by-label` then answers how many changes needed their spec, design or plan reworked after the stage that wrote it, the rework a label on a found issue never sees because it lands as commits inside the change. Decided 2026-09-24 with D-06 (asdlc-openspec-6dn), after the same second opinion showed that the calculator change's largest corrections, its spec revised during build and its design amended at verify, became no issue.
seenLabelPrefixMeans: The prefix of the label that counts how many runs have found an issue: the prefix and a whole number from 2 up, the run that filed the issue counted as the first, so an issue with no such label was found once. An issue carries one such label at most: one `bd update` takes `--remove-label` for the old number and `--add-label` for the next. `CLAUDE.md` § The task store says when a run raises it. The count is evidence for a person choosing what to work next, read with `bd show`, `bd list --label-regex` or `bd count --by-label`, and moves no priority by itself (`CLAUDE.md` § A program proposes; only a person promotes). A match before 2026-10-05 was noted and not counted, and no issue was recounted from its notes, so an older issue's count can be low. Renaming the prefix strands every count already on an issue: relabel them in the same change. Where it loses: two runs that match one issue at the same time both read the same label and both write the next number, so one match goes uncounted; each run's note still records it, and a recount from the notes corrects it. Decided 2026-10-05 with D-43 (asdlc-openspec-4myz): the maintainer chose a label over a metadata key and over a count derived from the notes, and evidence only over a row of `issuePriorities` that a count would move.
